newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to keep 97 budget gap at 3 pct or less - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to keep 97 budget gap at 3 pct or less - IMF.

text.p: Croatia is likely to keep its 1997 central budget deficit at three percent or under, International Monetary Fund (IMF) chief of mission Robert Feldman said on Tuesday.
"We reviewed the budget and are satisfied that the calculation shows that indeed the outcome can be within these limits," he told reporters.
The government proposed an almost 40 billion kuna budget for next year, envisaging the projected gap at 2.63 percent which is to be financed by external and domestic borrowing.

Feldman said the budget, which is expected to be passed by the country's parliament this week, had to make provisions for very different considerations, including development, social policy and income issues.
But he made no mention of fiscal plans for the next three years Croatia had to draw up as part of the economic policy for the duration of a new extended fund facility (EFF).
These were outlined in the past among the reasons it has taken authorities so long to strike a deal with the fund since a previous stand-by loan for economic stabilisation expired last spring.

In aid of further economic reforms, Croatia may draw on a total of $450-$500 million between 1997 and 1999 under the new arrangement, hoped to be approved in March or April next year. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
